entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: The Sankore Madrasah in Timbuktu, reaching its height under the Songhai Empire (15th–16th century), was West Africa's greatest center of Islamic scholarship. With an estimated 25,000 students and collections exceeding 700,000 manuscripts, it taught theology, astronomy, mathematics, law, and medicine. The Timbuktu manuscripts remain one of the world's most important yet understudied archives.
